evidence: STRUCTURE (source, supports a graded reward): tests/scoring.toml gates render/constraints at 0.0, weights functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2, floor functional 0.05 (identical to rules/projects/webdev-task-template/tests/scoring.toml; score.py and test.sh are byte-identical to the template). Gates are deliberately thin: render = load, nothing private before sign-in, wrong password refused, gwen signs in (tests/gates/render/judge.toml:25-34); constraints = post one message, reload, read it from a second context (tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:25-37). No scored difficulty sits in a gate, so a gate is not an all-or-nothing trap for an otherwise working chat app. Functional (tests/scored/functional/judge.toml) is weighted_mean over 16 independent binary criteria judged in mode='individual' (one session per criterion), weights 3,2,2,2,1.5,4,2,2,1.5,1.5,1.5,1.5,2.5,1.5,2.5,2 = 33 total; polish is weighted_mean of 5 binary 1.0 criteria; visual is weighted_mean of 4 likert/5-point criteria with anchors 0-5 (weights 2,2,1,1). The functional prompt (prompt.md:56-57) says 'Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure'. The only shared preconditions are sign-in and posting, both already gated. Distinct feature families (server-side refusals via replay, live polling, copy-link control, idempotent send, restart durability) each feed only a subset of criteria, so failures do not collapse together. ANALYTIC SPREAD (paper computation from the weights, NOT a measurement): (a) UI-complete app with client-side-only enforcement fails the replay-refusal criteria signin_and_client_scope 3, wall_every_route 2, wall_added_live 2, deleted_and_expired 4, timer_changes 2, hold_scope 2, edits 1.5, sent_once 2.5 and keeps about 14/33 = 0.42 functional; (b) app without live push/polling loses wall_added_live, unread, live_updates = 5/33, functional about 0.85; (c) a bare chat that passes only persistence (durability-only, judge.toml:251-270) gets 2/33 = 0.061 > floor; polish and visual add gradated mass on top. A dead/static app is zeroed by the constraints gate and a polish-only app by the 0.05 floor, which is the intended shaping. CAVEATS: (1) floor cliff: the smallest functional weight 1.5/33 = 0.0455 < 0.05, so an app passing exactly one 1.5-weight criterion scores reward 0 despite polish/visual (minor discontinuity; floor value is template-controlled). (2) Criteria are heavily conjunctive (e.g. deleted_and_expired_messages weight 4.0 = 12% of functional with Part A 4 legs + Part B), which coarsens granularity for near-miss apps; the spread for a target model could cluster low. (3) test.sh:224-226: if the whole scored suite exceeds its 11100 s budget, the reward stays at the gate-stage 0 for every dimension; nominal budgets are 16x550 + 900 + 900 = 10600 s, so this is an all-or-nothing tail only if judge timeouts are not honoured. MEASUREMENT: qc/runs/kittle-2026-10-09-r4/raw-evidence-index.json scope states verbatim 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' I re-verified all listed hashes (run_golden.sh b61aa378..., functional.cjs 980c6095..., golden-run.log b2fb05f4..., functional-before 4329fca7..., functional-after 2177dcb4..., restart-pids b0c412c9...) and the matching_source_files hashes against the frozen task (app.js 8fc558c9..., server.js 03b52651..., solve.sh f7c17a01..., seed f69616e2...): all match. That evidence is only a scripted Playwright golden all-pass (all 16 functional checks + gate_constraints + polish_refusal_in_place True); it shows the top end only and contains no partial-quality or mutated app and no configured judge run. No measured spread across partial apps exists, so per SKILL.md ('Never upgrade an unmeasured claim to Pass') and REVIEW_POLICY.md (reward discrimination needs a hash-bound runtime record) this row cannot be Pass. No demonstrated design defect blocks it.
counterexample: Not a Fail. Unmeasured scenarios to exercise: a weak app passing exactly one 1.5-weight functional criterion plus full polish/visual scores reward 0.0 (floor cliff), while one passing a 2.0 criterion scores about 0.44; and a near-complete app whose replays or live waits exceed the 550 s individual-criterion budget under the configured GLM judge could collapse many criteria to 0 regardless of quality.
suggested_fix: Produce a hash-bound reward-discrimination record: run the full configured verifier (or at minimum the scripted harness mapped to criterion weights) on the golden plus 3-4 mutated apps (e.g. client-side-only enforcement, no live polling, no idempotent send, bare chat) and record the resulting functional/polish/visual/reward values showing an ordered spread; optionally note the 1.5/33 < 0.05 floor cliff in the record.
